paragraphs: This project is a Streamlit-based web application that demonstrates different algorithms to generate the string "Hello, World!" with varying computational complexities. It serves as both an educational tool and a benchmarking suite to compare the performance of creative, humorous, and intentionally over-engineered approaches to a simple task.
Created by Kai Roth. For more details, visit the project repository.
features: 10 Unique Algorithms: Ranging from a simple direct return (O(1)) to a highly inefficient Bogo Sort permutation (O(n · n!) average case), showcasing a spectrum of computational complexities.
Interactive UI: Select algorithms via a slider, run benchmarks, and view intermediate steps, final results, and performance metrics.
Performance Metrics: Measures execution time and peak memory usage using Python's tracemalloc and time.perfcounter.
Theoretical Complexity: Displays Big-O time and space complexities for each algorithm.
Explanations and Code Snippets: Provides simplified explanations and code examples for educational purposes.
